title: Impact of US Export Controls on Singapore's Semi-conductor Industry and Ensuring Singapore-based Chip Companies Abide by New Rules to Safeguard Country's Business Reputation
what_it_is: Impact of US Export Controls on Singapore's Semi-conductor Industry and Ensuring Singapore-based Chip Companies Abide by New Rules to Safeguard Country's Business Reputation

sections.label: US chip export controls questions
sections.summary: Questions ask how Singapore prevents companies bypassing US trade restrictions and about US chip export control effects on Singapore's semiconductor industry and economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how does the Ministry ensure that the ease of doing business in Singapore is not exploited by companies seeking to bypass US trade restrictions; and (b) whether the Ministry can provide an update on its assessment of the effects of the US chips export control rules on our semi-conductor industry and the broader economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the Ministry is aware that Singapore will be placed under the new US AI export controls' Tier Two status; (b) whether it is a specific foreign policy objective of this Government to secure (i) the National Validated End-User status and (ii) Tier One reclassification under these controls; and (c) what specific technical and regulatory enhancements, if any, have been communicated by US counterparts as prerequisites for such status changes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry in light of how US agencies have flagged Singapore as a hub for illicit chip transshipments to blacklisted Chinese AI firms (a) whether the Government is able to (i) disclose the foreign policy rationales behind its regulatory stance with regard to re-exports of such chips since 2023 and (ii) detail any or all inter-agency decisions that led to this situation; and (b) how does the Government intend to rectify any damage to Singapore’s credibility and ties with the US arising from such reports.

sections.label: Nvidia Singapore sales scrutiny
sections.summary: Checks indicate physical delivery of products sold by Nvidia to Singapore is less than 1% of Nvidia's overall revenue.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are scrutinising this issue carefully and will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So far, our checks indicate that physical delivery of products sold by Nvidia to Singapore represent less than 1% of Nvidia's overall revenue.

sections.label: No legal duty on foreign controls
sections.summary: Singapore has no legal obligation to enforce other countries' unilateral export controls but expects companies to consider applicable regulations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: While we currently do not have legal obligations to enforce the unilateral export controls of other countries, we expect all companies operating in Singapore to take into account such regulations if they apply to their international business activities.

sections.label: US controls and Singapore chips
sections.summary: US technology controls target a narrow subset of advanced chips while Singapore focuses on mature node chips, and Singapore is classified Tier Two.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The US' current technology controls are aimed at a narrow subset of advanced semi-conductor chips, whereas Singapore's semi-conductor industry focuses on producing mature node chips which are used globally in appliances, automotives and industrial equipment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Singapore, like around 150 countries, has been classified as Tier Two.

sections.label: Strategic Goods Control Act regimes
sections.summary: The Strategic Goods (Control) Act 2002 regulates transfer and brokering of strategic goods, aligned with four multilateral export control regimes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Strategic Goods (Control) Act 2002 and its subsidiary legislation governs and regulates the transfer and brokering of strategic goods and technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Singapore's list of control goods and technologies is aligned with four multilateral export control regimes, namely the Wassenaar Arrangement, the Australia Group, the Missile Technology Control Regime and the Nuclear Suppliers Group.

sections.label: Nvidia SEC filing revenue figures
sections.summary: Nvidia's SEC filing states US$91 billion total revenue for nine months ended October 2024, with a little less than half domestic to the US.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding Minister Tan's assertions about the physical sales of Nvidia products being only around 1%, Nvidia's latest filing with the US Securities Exchange Commission states that for the nine months that ended October 2024, the company booked US$91 billion in total revenue, of which a little less than half is domestic; that is, domestic to the US.

sections.label: MFA review of MTI trade decisions
sections.summary: The Member asks whether MFA has a formal mechanism to review or input into MTI trade decisions with foreign policy implications, and asks MTI what steps it will take after Singapore's Tier Two US status.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And relatedly, is there a formal mechanism for MFA to review or provide input to MTI's trade decisions that have inevitable foreign policy implications?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And finally, one question directly for MTI, and given that Singapore is now being placed under Tier Two status by the US, what specific steps will the Government take or plan to take to prevent further downgrades of our status, which could jeopardise our AI hub aspirations?

sections.label: Nvidia sales booked to Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker says Nvidia reported 22% of chip sales booked to entities with operations in Singapore, but only 1% physically came to Singapore and was deployed in data centres here.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: These unique characteristics are par for the course for the unique role that Singapore plays in the global economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, for instance, when, as the Member correctly said, Nvidia states in its returns that 22% of sales of chips were booked to entities with operations in Singapore, but my colleague has already explained to the Member only 1% physically came to Singapore and was deployed in data centres here, serving the Government and other major enterprises, including, I should add, hyperscalers.

sections.label: Enforcing multilateral export control regimes
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore is not legally obliged to enforce 200 countries' unilateral export measures but will enforce multilaterally agreed export control regimes, and will not allow companies to use Singapore's association to evade unilateral measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is possible for 200 countries to promulgate unilateral export measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have explained that we are not legally obliged to enforce that unilateral export measures of 200 countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But we will enforce the multilateral agreed-upon export control regimes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Having said that, it is not in our national interest to be made use of and for companies who, for whatever reasons, are trying perhaps to evade unilateral export control measures that apply to them, to use their association with Singapore – because people know Singapore is a clean, hygienic, transparent and reputable place – we will not allow them to use that association with us to engage in deceptive or evasive measures to avoid unilateral export measures that apply to them.

sections.label: Nvidia quarterly revenue attributed to Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker addresses Assoc Prof Lim's point on Nvidia's quarterly revenue, stating that in the third quarter of 2024, 22% of Nvidia's quarterly revenue was attributed to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I want to also address Assoc Prof Lim's point about Nvidia's quarterly revenue, as he shared earlier on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I just wanted to put it into very clear perspective for the Member: in the third quarter of 2024, the proportion of Nvidia's quarterly revenue attributed to Singapore is 22%.

sections.label: Nvidia revenue physically shipped to Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker says global entities commonly centralise billing in their hubs, separate from where products are shipped, and checks show less than 1% of Nvidia's overall revenue that quarter was physically shipped into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It is common practice for global entities to centralise the billing for procured goods and services in their hubs, but this is separate from where the products are shipped to.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So far, from our checks and the data that we have on hand, it is revealed that in that quarter, less than 1% of Nvidia's overall revenue was physically shipped into Singapore.

sections.label: Date of 13 January 2025
sections.summary: The speaker states that the date was 13 January 2025, just over a month ago.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Actually, it is on 13 January 2025, just over a month ago.

sections.label: Imported chips and national cap
sections.summary: Chips imported by universal and national verified end users do not count towards the national cap on Tier Two countries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Chips that are imported by both universal and national verified end users will not count towards the national cap imposed on Tier Two countries.
